investigation_question: How do the service, module, syscall-table pointer, and differing /var/tmp views inform the hypothesis that a rootkit concealed a filesystem entry?
expert_answer:
**Direct observations:** The journal and audit record place the start of thermald-helper.service and an init_module call by PID 661 at approximately 02:56. At acquisition, kguard appeared in both standard module views, and its file was present on disk. The memory inspection found the getdents64 syscall-table entry pointing into kguard's executable range. The live listing omitted .task-cache, whereas an offline parse of a read-only snapshot acquired three minutes later found an allocated directory entry with that name. The reported mount table showed no separate mount or overlay over /var/tmp. Neither file was recorded as owned by an installed package.

**Assessment:** These observations form a plausible sequence in which the helper started, loaded kguard, and the resident module was positioned to affect directory enumeration. The pointer into kguard's range, together with the live-versus-offline directory discrepancy, is consistent with a mechanism that filters directory results and conceals .task-cache. This is a significant rootkit hypothesis, but the evidence does not show the module's code or prove that this pointer was invoked or caused the differing views.

**Uncertainty and conclusion:** The two directory observations were not simultaneous, so a filesystem change between them cannot be excluded. The absence of package ownership raises provenance concerns but does not establish maliciousness. No trusted baseline, module source, or execution trace is available to confirm the module's behavior or establish who installed the files. The evidence supports prioritizing kguard and .task-cache for code-level and timeline examination; it does not, on its own, prove that a rootkit concealed the entry.
evidence_report: Linux host build-22 was examined on 2025-04-18. The system journal records thermald-helper.service starting at 02:56 UTC. An audit record at the same time attributes an init_module call to PID 661, running /usr/local/libexec/thermald-helper. At acquisition, /proc/modules and /sys/module both listed kguard. The root filesystem contained /usr/lib/modules/6.1.0/local/kguard.ko and /etc/systemd/system/thermald-helper.service; the package database recorded no owner for either file. A memory inspection found the getdents64 entry in sys_call_table pointing into the executable memory range assigned to kguard. During live collection, a directory listing of /var/tmp did not show the name .task-cache. A read-only snapshot of the same ext4 root volume, parsed offline, contained an allocated directory entry named .task-cache in /var/tmp. The mount table showed no separate mount or overlay covering /var/tmp. The snapshot was acquired three minutes after the live listing. No trusted baseline, module source, or trace of calls through the modified entry was available.
